I've been farming these 8 mu for 40 years now, since I was 25. I'm 65, so I don't move as fast as I used to, but I know every corner of this land. There are five of us at home — my wife, my son, my daughter-in-law, my grandson, and me. My son and daughter-in-law both work in Shijiazhuang, so it's mostly my wife and me doing the farm work, though my daughter helps during harvest when she can get leave from the factory.

I keep 6 mu in wheat-maize double cropping and 2 mu in cotton. I need the cotton for some cash income diversification, but it's too labor-intensive to do more than 2 mu with just the two of us.

**For wheat**, I'm planting in mid-October with the Jinmai 47 variety I've used for years. It costs about 35 yuan per mu for seed. I plow and rotary till before planting, then put down base fertilizer — about 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, which gives me roughly 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium. The extension fellow told me I could go up to 18 kg nitrogen, but I tried 13 kg on one plot two years ago and the yield dropped a bit, so I'm back to 15 kg. Better safe than sorry — a bad wheat year hurts more than saving a few yuan on fertilizer helps. I'll topdress with about 5 kg of urea at jointing in March if the wheat looks yellow. I irrigate three times: wintering water before freeze-up, then at jointing, and once at grain filling. The well water is metered now, so each irrigation costs about 20 yuan per mu. For pesticides, I spray herbicide after planting and watch for aphids in spring, same as my neighbor Lao Zhang.

**For maize**, it goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June. Sometimes I only have 4 or 5 days before I miss the planting window. I hire Old Wang's tractor for no-till planting — costs me 30 yuan per mu but saves time and labor. I use hybrid seed, about 3.5 kg per mu at 55 yuan. I put all the fertilizer down at planting — about 45 kg compound fertilizer per mu, giving 14 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 2 kg potassium. One irrigation in July if it doesn't rain. Maize is easier to manage than wheat, and the hybrid varieties are reliable.

**For cotton**, I plant in late April on the 2 mu. Cotton needs more pesticide — herbicide, insecticide for bollworms, sometimes fungicide if the weather is wet. I use about 40 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base, then topdress another round at flowering in July. Two irrigations, usually in June and August. The real problem with cotton is the picking — it's all manual, very labor intensive. My wife and I pick most of it over three rounds, but I hire 4 days of labor to help because at my age, bending down to pick cotton all day is hard on my back.

Total input costs — seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation, tractor hire, and hired labor — will be about 4,200 yuan this year. I have about 5,000 yuan saved from last year, so I can manage, but I need to keep some cash for emergencies. My son sends money home for my grandson's school fees, so I don't want to ask him for more. That's why I'm not increasing fertilizer even though the extension agent says I could — I know what works on my land, and I can't afford to gamble.
